parties: PI Industries Limited (parent) and PI Health Sciences Limited (wholly owned subsidiary)
headline: PI Industries exercises conversion of OFCD into equity in subsidiary PI Health Sciences
sum: PI Industries has exercised its conversion option on Optionally Fully Convertible Debentures (OFCDs) issued by wholly owned subsidiary PI Health Sciences Limited, converting them into equity shares. The move consolidates the capital structure within the PI Industries group.
implication: Conversion of OFCDs by a parent into equity of a wholly owned subsidiary raises questions on whether the conversion triggers fresh valuation, arm's-length pricing scrutiny under related-party transaction rules, and whether the subsidiary's updated cap table requires shareholder approval or stamp duty re-assessment under the Indian Stamp Act.
detail: PI Industries Limited, a publicly listed pharmaceutical company, exercised a contractual conversion right embedded in Optionally Fully Convertible Debentures that had been issued by its 100%-owned subsidiary, PI Health Sciences Limited. The conversion of debt into equity alters the subsidiary's ownership structure and capitalisation. No acquisition of external assets or third-party stake is involved; this is an intra-group reorganisation. The specific number of shares into which the debentures were converted, and the date of conversion, are not disclosed in the NSE notification.

framework.note: central - definition and regulation of subsidiary; conversion transaction does not trigger MCA approval under 'acquisition' unless the subsidiary issues new shares to third parties post-conversion

central - related-party transaction framework; parent–subsidiary debenture conversion may fall under Schedule V if material, requiring independent director/shareholder approval depending on materiality threshold

framework.ref: SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, Reg. 30 & Schedule III, Part A
framework.note: central - listed entity (PI Industries) must disclose material related-party transactions or acquisitions; NSE filing confirms disclosure obligation met
amended - stamp duty on conversion of debentures into equity; recent clarifications suggest conversion may attract fresh stamp duty on the underlying consideration, depending on state interpretation
central - transfer pricing provisions for related-party transactions; if conversion value exceeds book value, may trigger arm's-length pricing scrutiny
- subsidiary capitalisation filings with Registrar of Companies; updated memorandum and articles reflecting post-conversion share capital must be filed within prescribed timeline

framework.ref: SEBI Prohibition of Insider Trading Regulation, 2015, Reg. 3 & 4
framework.note: - trading window closure and insider list management during OFCD conversion announcement and execution period; PI Industries must ensure compliance

structure.novel: Intra-group conversion of unlisted subsidiary debt to equity; subsidiary remains 100%-owned post-conversion. No external valuation or third-party stake acquisition.
